quote: I wanted to add panels and possibly a battery.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers interest in expanding his existing system with a battery — a live cross-sell/upsell signal (Tesla Powerwall) that the rep should have flagged.
coaching_implication: Rep should reflect this back: 'Great, we'll make sure the specialist walks you through battery options too' — instead moved straight to a Google Maps tree question.

quote: on Google Maps, it shows you have a pretty large tree in your backyard. Is that tree removed?
stewart_read: Rep captures the shading/tree fact and moves on procedurally instead of using it to build curiosity ('so getting those panels repositioned could actually help output').
alternative_hypothesis: Could be intentional scope discipline (leaving analysis to closer) but the line is delivered as pure data-gathering, not a deliberate defer-and-hook.
coaching_implication: Even a brief acknowledgment ('that's probably limiting your output — worth having the specialist look at repositioning') would create forward pull.

stewart_read: The customer pushes back on the stated $200/month figure — a moment ripe for the objection_inversion flip ('that's actually the number working against you') — rep instead just restates and drops it.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the driving customer wasn't in a state to engage with a flip, deferring the pitch to the specialist visit — but nothing in the transcript shows deliberate strategy, just a shrug-and-move-on.
coaching_implication: Line should have gone: 'That's actually the number we want to fix — that's money going straight to Pepco.' Instead rep said 'A little high, I would say.'

quote: So it would be best to, pick up this conversation once I once I get home in a couple hours.
stewart_read: Call ends with no locked callback time, no appointment date/time, no verbal handshake — a fully open-ended deferral.
coaching_implication: Rep should have proposed a specific time: 'Perfect, how about I call you back at 5 today once you're home?' instead of accepting 'a couple hours' as-is.

quote: Okay. Were you just, like, re inquiring like, were you wanting to add panels or a battery or anything?
stewart_read: Rep runs the orphaned-system flow but skips probing who the original installer relationship/experience was like or why he's expanding now — moves straight to logistics.
alternative_hypothesis: Given call brevity and driving customer, this could be deliberate scope trimming rather than a miss.
coaching_implication: A quick 'what's driving the addition — bill still too high even with the existing system?' would have tied straight into the bill anchor later.

quote: just a copy of your kilowatt usage. That way we can determine how many more panels you'll need.
stewart_read: Rep asks for the bill but never ties it back to the earlier 'sounds a little high' pushback or the battery interest — a missed chance to reinforce both anchors at once.
coaching_implication: Combine asks: 'Since that $200 sounded high and you're already thinking about a battery, this usage data will show us exactly how much more we can offset.'
